I hate people who say postmodernism means everything is subjective and therefore all views are equal. That's not right. I think postmodernism is actually about humility and doubt and questioning. There is something that deeply resonates in postmodernism, which is the deconstruction of the narrative. We live in a constructed world and we tend to take that for granted. We tend to see what we see and the reality that's been constructed and think that's reality. And then postmodernism says, "Hey, let's take a step back and deconstruct this narrative. Look at the underside of it. See who's doing the construction and how they construct it and why. Why is this the way it is? What is being left out? What is being excluded?" So, it's actually a really critical and skeptical look at things. It doesn't mean that nothing is real, that there is no truth, it's just saying let's really look at all the angles and see how all these stories and narratives get constructed.
A good example of postmodernism is the way we view Hollywood films now, the canon of what makes a good movie, is postmodern in the sense that we have really lost the early 20th century obsession with realistic film. So now we have very fantastical movies that are making lots of money, but they're not really trying to tell you what real life is. They are trying to give you some postmodern kind of existential, magical realism or fantasy. And that's postmodern. When you deconstruct reality, the stuff that's real in the real world is only some tiny fraction of what's real. There's imaginary things, there's fantasy, there's dreams, there's ideas, there's thoughts. So, we stop being so obsessed with the realism of narrative. We are actually more comfortable with fantastical movies. So, that's the deconstruction of the narrative. So, it's a very interesting area of thought, and I think it's very useful to be postmodern in the sense that you're not just taking what's given to you at face value. And you're not letting people convince you that this narrative is the only narrative, the one and true narrative. But there's different narratives. And also postmodernism is very self-reflexive. It's very self aware. It's like, "Yeah, I am aware of what I am doing. I am aware that I'm constructing this narrative in this specific way." And it's really beautiful when writers do that. I really appreciate self-reflexive writing that's very self aware that it is constructing a narrative and it doesn't take it for granted. That's very postmodern. I really love that.
